KEY MESSAGE 1...Scattered severe thunderstorms will continue to
track southeastward across portions of eastern PA, NJ, and 
perhaps the Delmarva through late this evening. Damaging wind 
gusts, large hail, and a tornado or two will be possible.

A Severe Thunderstorm Watch remains in effect for the entire 
area until midnight tonight. 

A quasi-stationary front is currently located just to the north
of the area. This evening, it should begin to work southward as
a cold front. Ahead of this boundary, the environment has 
become characterized by strong instability, with MLCAPE values 
as high as 3000 J/kg. Deep layer shear is generally on the order
of 40-45 kt to the south of the frontal boundary. 

Despite nebulous forcing, scattered thunderstorms, some severe,
have developed across portions of eastern PA into northern NJ. 
This activity will spread southeastward through late this 
evening. Given the strong instability and shear, a mix of 
supercells and line segments will continue to be the storm mode.
Some guidance suggests upscale growth into a QLCS, but so far 
this has yet to occur and it is not guaranteed. Damaging winds 
and a few instances of severe hail are the expected primary 
hazards. However, a tornado or two cannot be ruled out with any 
supercells as ESRH is on the order of 100-125 m2/s2. 

Storms should clear the region by midnight or shortly after. 
Once the front works its way through the area, much of the 
overnight period tonight will be dry. However, the marine layer 
will spread inland across much of the area leading to widespread
low clouds. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...On Wednesday, a shortwave trough could spark another 
round of showers and storms, but it will be working against a 
relatively stable boundary layer.

In the wake of the storms Tuesday Night, the front is expected to 
sink back south of the region by Wednesday morning, leaving our 
region in the relatively cooler and more stable air mass north of 
the front. The net result is that our region should be in 
northeasterly flow, and relatively cloudy conditions for much of the 
day. As a result, surface-based instability is going to be almost 
non-existent, though model soundings do show elevated instability 
for parcels above 900 mb. 

Consequently, the risk for severe storms is still quite conditional 
and uncertain. Given how sharp of a mid level short wave trough is 
approaching, there will be ample forcing, but it is a question of if 
the elevated instability will be enough to sustain storms in our 
region.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Hot and humid conditions are forecast across the 
region on Thursday. 

After a cool down on Wednesday for most neighborhoods (5 to 10 
degrees lower - less across Delmarva), hot and humid conditions are 
once again expected across the region on Thursday as the frontal 
boundary lifts north. With the front to the north, high temperatures 
are forecast to climb into the upper 80s to mid 90s for many areas 
(around 80 or low 80s far N and W). These temperatures combined with 
dewpoints in the low to mid 70s will again result in heat indices 
well into the 90s to low 100s south of I-78, perhaps even as high as 
105 degrees for Delmarva.

Another Heat Advisory may be needed for portions of the area on
Thursday if this trend continues.

KEY MESSAGE 4...Unsettled conditions will continue on Thursday with 
the potential for severe thunderstorms. Scattered thunderstorms are 
again possible on Friday, mainly from Philadelphia south.

Another round of severe thunderstorms are possible on Thursday. 
Friday could also experience a few severe storms across Delmarva, 
depending on how quickly the frontal boundary pushes south.

SPC has a Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for severe thunderstorms 
on Thursday from about Wilmington to Wildwood NJ southward and a 
Marginal Risk (level 1) to the north of this. 

The northwest flow pattern will remain in place on Thursday and will 
continue to be supportive of all severe threats, including damaging 
winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes, depending on how all the 
mesoscale details pan out. The threat for flash flooding is 
typically lower with these patterns, but not zero. Training can 
still occur and a single locale could have multiple days with heavy 
rainfall.

Friday's SPC's 15% probabilities for severe thunderstorms have 
shifted just south of our Delmarva zones, though there is still some 
uncertainty with this. Our latest forecast has about a 30-40% chance 
of showers and thunderstorms south of about Philadelphia.

KEY MESSAGE 5...The Labor Day Weekend will feature mostly dry 
weather with at or below normal temperatures and lower humidity.

By Saturday, current model consensus indicates the frontal boundary 
will be pushing south of our region with Canadian high pressure
